content: Combines BFL upper and lower bounds into a single sandwich: for any ε > 0, eventually n^{3/2-ε} ≤ f(n) ≤ n^{3/2+ε}. This is the strongest known result about the triangle removal process.
The full Erdős conjecture Θ(n^{3/2}) is equivalent to having both an upper Θ-bound (f(n) ≤ C·n^{3/2}) and a lower Θ-bound (c·n^{3/2} ≤ f(n)) holding simultaneously.
The BFL exponent is exactly 3/2: for any α > 3/2, we get f(n) ≤ n^α eventually. This is proved by substituting ε = α - 3/2 into the BFL upper bound.
The complete graph K_n for n ≥ 3 contains a triangle. Proved by constructing the explicit triangle (0, 1, 2) in Fin n using Fin.mk.
If f(n)/n^{3/2} converges to a positive limit L, the full Erdős conjecture holds. This reduces the conjecture to a convergence question about a single ratio.
